alt: Three early portrait interface directions for the small e-paper display
caption: The first screen concepts assumed portrait orientation. The actual desk did not agree.

alt: First landscape screen layout with remaining usage, reset timing, and reset credits
caption: The first landscape pass established the basic information hierarchy.

alt: Landscape screen revision with a last refresh timestamp beneath the usage bar
caption: Adding the last-refresh time made stale data visible instead of merely suspicious.

alt: Approved display mock with remaining usage on the left and reset information on the right
caption: The approved mock still put the percentage on the left and reset information on the right.

alt: Implemented hardware layout with reset information on the left and remaining usage on the right
caption: Elecrow's mirrored landscape X-axis sent the two columns to opposite sides on the physical panel. The result worked, so it became the real layout.

alt: Early bulky easel-style enclosure concept
caption: The first enclosure was an easel. It was also far too much enclosure for this amount of screen.

alt: First CAD pass for a picture-frame enclosure with a removable side piece
caption: The first picture-frame CAD pass introduced the removable side stile.

alt: Thinner-rim CAD revision with an offset right side
caption: The bezel got leaner, but the right-side shoulder still looked like an unexplained accident.

alt: Measured asymmetric frame proposal with the right edge wider than the other sides
caption: We tried making one side wider instead of adding a shoulder. Better, still not the final answer.

alt: Rear CAD view showing the right-angle USB-C cable routed through the stand
caption: The right-angle cable needed a real path through the bottom and out the back.

alt: Purple CAD rendering of the assembled frame, display, back, and leg
caption: The first complete parametric assembly looked extremely plausible on a screen. Physical reality was waiting.

alt: CAD rendering of the four original printable enclosure parts
caption: V1 went to the printer as four parts: frame, backplate, side stile, and leg.

alt: First enclosure print beginning on the textured Bambu build plate
caption: The first physical enclosure began face-down on the textured plate.

alt: The four pieces from the first print laid out on a desk
caption: All four V1 pieces printed cleanly. Nothing meaningful retained them.

alt: First printed enclosure propped beneath the monitor from the seated viewing position
caption: The taped-together V1 established the real scale and showed that the frame needed a backward lean.

alt: V2 enclosure pieces completed on the textured build plate
caption: V2 made the front continuous and moved more structure into the back.

alt: V2 frame held up to show failed unsupported strands inside one edge
caption: Unsupported geometry supplied the inevitable serving of purple spaghetti.

alt: V2 frame and rear pieces shown from the front
caption: The seamless front was right. The retention strategy and internal depth were not.

alt: CAD view of the deeper V3 rear cavity and magnetic backplate
caption: V3 rebuilt the rear around measured hardware depth and a magnetic cover.

alt: CAD side view of the enclosure leaning back at 60 degrees from the desk
caption: The corrected posture put the display 60 degrees from the desk, finally leaning the useful direction.

alt: Front CAD view of the uninterrupted symmetric V3 frame
caption: The front became one quiet, symmetric piece aligned to the active pixels.

alt: V3 frame, backplate, and leg beginning on the textured build plate
caption: V3 reduced the enclosure to three printable parts.

alt: The three completed V3 enclosure parts arranged on the desk
caption: The completed V3 parts: seamless frame, magnetic backplate, and removable leg.

alt: Close front view of the V3 frame showing its textured plate finish
caption: Printing face-down gave the bezel the build plate's texture. Good, but busier than I wanted at this scale.

alt: V3 frame, magnets, and cyanoacrylate glue arranged for installation
caption: The first magnetic retention test began with very tiny magnets and a deeply unhelpful amount of superglue.

alt: Hand-held V3 enclosure demonstrating excess space behind the screen
caption: Then we discovered the cavity was too generous. The display could fall away from the front window.

alt: Side view of a three-magnet test stack leaving the V3 rear cover slightly proud
caption: Three stacked magnets proved the pocket depth was off by approximately one printed layer.

alt: V3 rear leg and USB-C cable shown where they meet the desk
caption: The viewing angle worked, but the leg touched on one corner and the cable tunnel needed more height.

alt: V4 enclosure printing face-down on the smooth build plate
caption: V4 moved to the smooth plate and corrected the cavity, feet, leg, cable tunnel, and magnet pockets.

alt: Completed V4 frame, backplate, and leg before magnet installation
caption: The finished V4 parts before magnets, with all four corner pockets visible.

alt: Four magnets being installed into the corners of the V4 frame
caption: Four frame magnets cured in the corrected corner pockets.

alt: V4 rear cover aligned over the frame during the second magnet-installation stage
caption: The mating magnets were aligned by letting the frame hold the rear cover in position.

alt: V4 frame and backplate separated with all eight magnets installed
caption: All eight magnets installed, with the frame and backplate finally behaving like one object.

alt: Side profile of the assembled V4 enclosure showing its backward lean
caption: The corrected feet and leg put the screen at the intended reading angle.

alt: Rear view of V4 showing the removable leg and USB-C cable tunnel
caption: The final rear geometry leaves a clear route for the right-angle USB-C cable.

alt: Finished powered purple e-paper display photographed from three quarters
caption: The finished object: smooth purple bezel, readable screen, magnetic back, and no unexplained shoulder.

alt: Finished Codex usage display beneath the monitor beside a small astronaut figure
caption: In its actual habitat under the monitor, quietly tattling on my remaining Codex budget.
